Success => exit 0, all output on stdout, nothing on stderr. - `prog` is taken from `os.path.basename(sys.argv[0])`, not hard-coded: invoking the same binary through a differently-named symlink changes every occurrence of the program name in usage/help/error text. - `-h` and `--help` print the help text to STDOUT (byte-identical for both spellings) and exit 0. The exact bytes at terminal width 80 are: `usage: test14_executable [-h] --a A --b B Complex markdown processing chain options: -h, --help show this help message and exit --a A --b B ` (149 bytes total, exactly one trailing newline, no trailing blank line). Note `options:` (Python >=3.10 wording, not `optional arguments:`). Help is on stdout, so `1>/dev/null` suppresses it entirely and stderr stays empty. - Help short-circuits: as soon as the `-h`/`--help` token is reached during the left-to-right scan, help is printed and the process exits 0 — required-argument checks and unrecognized-argument checks never run. There is no ambiguity anywhere in this parser: no two option strings share a common prefix, so the "ambiguous option" error is unreachable. `--a` and `--b` are already exact matches and have no longer counterparts. - Option names are case-sensitive and single-dash spellings are NOT accepted: `-a`, `-b`, `--A`, `--B` are not recognized as `--a`/`--b`. (`-a` fails single-dash prefix matching because `'--a'.startswith('-a')` is false.) They become unrecognized option tokens, so parsing proceeds without setting --a/--b and the missing-required error fires first. - Both space-separated (`--a X`) and `=`-attached (`--a=X`) forms are accepted, in any order, and `--b Y --a X` is equivalent to `--a X --b Y`. With the `=` form, only the FIRST `=` is the separator; all remaining characters (including further `=`) are part of the value. `--a=` yields the empty string, exactly like `--a ''`. - Duplicate flags: action is `store`, so the LAST occurrence wins (each occurrence overwrites the namespace attribute). Names are listed in declaration order (`--a` before `--b`) and joined with `, `. Both-missing => `--a, --b`; only-b-missing => `--b`; only-a-missing => `--a`. - Missing value after a flag (flag is last token, or the next token is classified as option-like): STDERR gets the usage line plus `: error: argument --a: expected one argument` (or `--b`), exit 2. The message names the option exactly as it was declared (`--a` / `--b`), not as typed. This error is raised at the moment the flag is consumed, i.e. before any missing-required or unrecognized-argument reporting. - Classification of a candidate value token T that begins with `-` (this decides between "T is the value" and "expected one argument").
